p0_findings.evidence: Exact M1228 result places configuration under selected.configuration; M1227 line 639 reads selection.configuration and raises KeyError.
p0_findings.impact: The final cross-run selection result cannot be consumed, so no release can be authored.

p0_findings.evidence: A recursively double-sealed result containing selected checkpoint/config-A plus conflicting top-level config-B is accepted; returned binding uses checkpoint/config-B and ignores selected.configuration.
p0_findings.impact: Double sealing proves bytes, not that checkpoint and config belong to the same selected candidate.

p0_findings.evidence: selection_schema is supplied by the future launch entry, selection status is not checked, and no independent final-selection result hammer is required.
p0_findings.impact: An unhammered result whose own status says hardware rebind is not authorized can pass after the top-level-config splice.

required_additive_repair: Read checkpoint and configuration from the same selected object; reject a top-level configuration key for the M1228 schema.
Pin the exact final-selection schema and exact admitted result-hammer authority in source/contract rather than accepting a schema string supplied by the launch JSON.
Require exact selected identity keys/types and bind selected candidate_id, epoch, profile, checkpoint and config to the independent result hammer.
Keep the already passing 259/247/live-dead/atomic/9880/480/640 contracts unchanged.
Use a fresh additive source revision and a new hammer; do not edit or relabel this M1227 evidence.
